evidence.excerpt: Deploying high-accuracy surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware—spanning microcontrollers, FPGAs, and GPU-equipped single-board computers—requires models that balance computational cost with detection performance across very different hardware profiles. This paper proposes a hardware-aware knowledge distillation pipeline in which a large teacher network transfers representational knowledge to a suite of student architectures of varying capacities, each targeting a specific hardware tier. A novel attention-alignment distillation loss aligns intermediate feature maps at multiple scales, preserving fine-grained defect discriminability in the student networks. Experiments on three industrial surface inspection datasets show that the distilled lightweight students retain 95–98% of teacher mAP while reducing multiply-accumulate operations by 4× to 11× depending on the target hardware. We further present a hardware profiling methodology that automates student architecture selection given user-defined latency and accuracy constraints. The complete pipeline is released as an open-source toolkit, enabling non-expert practitioners to generate inspection-ready models for their specific edge deployment targets.
